transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. This is a water-and-electricity hazard, so treat it as urgent. The dishwasher must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it. The usual causes are a leak at the door (seal, door alignment or a spray arm directing water at it), a loose/split inlet or drain hose, or an internal leak such as a pump seal or hose. If there is lots of foam, washing-up liquid or excess detergent can force foam and water out of the door. Only with the dishwasher isolated at the consumer unit, and without touching wet sockets, plugs or leads:
1. Keep people away from the wet area; mop up water only if you can do so without going near the sockets.
2. Look for the water’s likely route: from the door edge, from the hoses/connections under the sink, or from underneath the dishwasher. This helps identify whether it is an external connection or an internal/door leak.
3. Look through the door for excessive foam. Foam points to detergent rather than a failed component. Do not run a test cycle or try to dry/reset it. Given the flooding and nearby sockets, book a dishwasher engineer; if water has reached a socket, include that in the call and have the electrical installation checked as well.
its still running tho!! theres loads of bubbles coming out the bottom of the door and the water is spreading towards an extension lead on the floor. should i just turn it off at the wall??

No — do not turn it off at the wall if water may be near the socket, plug or extension lead. Do not touch the extension lead either. If you can reach the consumer unit without going through the water, switch off the dishwasher circuit there; if you cannot identify that circuit, switch off the main switch. If it is not safe to reach the consumer unit, keep away from the area and call an emergency electrician. The dishwasher must not be used again until it and the affected electrical area have been checked. The bubbles coming from the bottom of the door make excess suds the leading possibility — usually washing-up liquid/hand soap, or too much detergent, has been used. Suds can force water past an otherwise sound door seal. A genuine door-seal, spray-arm or internal leak is still possible, but do not investigate or run another cycle while there is water near electrical equipment.
ok i can reach the fuse box without going thru the water i think. theres no rcd trip tho. housemate squirted fairy liquid in cos we ran out of tablets, is that why? what do i do after i switch it off

Yes. Fairy liquid is very likely why: it makes far more foam than dishwasher detergent, and that foam can be forced out at the bottom of the door. It does not mean a pump or door seal has necessarily failed. Switch off the dishwasher circuit at the consumer unit now, provided you can reach it without crossing the wet area. Do not touch the wall switch, plug, socket or extension lead while there is any chance they are wet. 1. Keep the dishwasher off and keep people away from the water and extension lead. Do not reconnect or use the extension lead.
2. Once the electrical area has been made safe, mop up water only where you can do so without approaching or handling sockets, plugs or leads. If water has reached, splashed into, or run under a socket or extension lead, arrange an electrician to check that electrical equipment.
3. Do not try an empty rinse, drain cycle or reset at this stage.
ok going to the fuse box now. after its off do i just leave it till the landlord sorts it? its his machine

Yes — once you have safely switched the circuit off at the consumer unit, leave the dishwasher off and let the landlord arrange the repair. Do not attempt to drain, rinse or restart it yourself, even though the Fairy liquid is the likely reason for the foam flooding out. Tell the landlord clearly that washing-up liquid was used, foam and water came out from the bottom of the door, and water spread towards an extension lead and nearby sockets. The dishwasher needs checking before it is used again. If water has reached the extension lead, its plug, or a socket, the affected electrical equipment also needs an electrician’s check; do not reuse that extension lead. The immediate cause is very likely excess suds, rather than a failed dishwasher part. After the area is electrically safe and the suds have been dealt with by the landlord/engineer, they can establish whether there is also a genuine door seal, spray-arm, hose or internal leak. Do not assume the appliance is safe simply because the foam eventually goes down.

candidates: Door-area leak, such as a dirty/damaged seal, misaligned door or spray being deflected at the door (medium)
Leaking inlet/drain hose connection or internal hose/pump seal (medium)
